thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 - multi-region failover anomaly detected. Symptoms: rising 5xx from us-east-1, traffic-shift job started to us-west-2 but shift not completing. Auto-escalate if not acknowledged in 5m. https://internal.incidents/3689012345

sylvie: ACK. I'm oncall. summary pls and current impact?

raj: Observed repeated ALB target health flaps in us-east-1-a starting ~+3m, other AZs degrade shortly after. The traffic-shift controller tried to move weights but connection pools and some edge caches kept hitting east. 5xx spike ~8% of requests in last 10m, mostly API write paths.

maria: I see control-plane errors in the region too — some route table updates failing with 504 from provider's control plane. Net telemetry shows increased retransmits inside us-east-1-a.

leo: Cloud provider alert: "fabric node rebooting" in us-east-1-a, they flagged packet loss to L3. They've marked ASG in that AZ as unhealthy. Contacting support now.

evan-cs: Any customer-facing impact so I can update CS? Getting 2 bug reports from larger tenants about timeouts.

raj: Quick impact estimate: ~8% of total token requests got 5xx, top tier customers show ~12% elevated latencies. No data plane leakage. No evidence of model correctness issues, purely network/transport.

maria: TTLs on DNS for region routing are 60s but many clients (mobile SDKs) cache longer. That explains why some traffic still hits east even after weight change.

leo: For immediate mitigation, propose: 1) Pause automated traffic-shift job 2) Force-route weight: set us-east region weight 0 at edge, 3) Increase connection drain timeout to 60s to avoid abrupt resets, 4) Scale up us-west backends to absorb surge. Anyone object?

sylvie: Do it. I'll take executor role. raj, can you run the forced weight change and scaling? maria, keep cloud-provider support loop open. evan update CS with "partial region outage affecting a subset of customers; mitigation in progress"

raj: Running weight change now. Command:```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZXXXXXXXX --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":0}}]}'
```

raj: Pushed. Also bumped target group deregistration delay:```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:tg:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=60
```

maria: Cloud support says fabric maintenance in us-east-1-a is ongoing; they recommend draining AZ and shifting traffic, but need us to confirm weight changes to avoid flapping. They're also seeing BGP adjacency renewals causing transient route churn to internet egress nodes.

leo: Noted. I've asked edge cache team to purge sticky routecache entries for region-based routing to accelerate clients switching. Command we used:```http
POST https://edge-api.internal/v1/cache/purge
{ "prefix": "/r/east/*" }
```

ev an-cs: CS update posted: "We're investigating partial outages impacting the East region. Mitigation started; some customers may see elevated errors or timeouts. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes or after status changes." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Automation note: traffic-shift job automatically paused by sylvie at +7m.

raj: Initial telemetry after forced weight change: 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 2.1% in 2 minutes. But a tail of stale clients still hitting east. Edge purge reduced that tail by ~60%.

maria: Provider says they will keep fabric node in maintenance for 1hr to apply patch. They've scheduled all VMs in that AZ to be proactively evacuated. If that completes, we can bring weight back incrementally.

sylvie: We're going to hold at forced weight 0 and monitor for 30m. I'll hand off to raj for next 2-hour watch. Handoff: sylvie -> raj. Raj, you're primary; sylvie reachable for escalations.

raj: Ack handoff. I'll watch dashboards, run golden health checks every 5m. Setting alert thresholds to lower to catch regressions.

evan-cs: Notifying top 5 customers with elevated impact. Will offer credits per SLA if we pass threshold. Any customers to mention specifically?

sylvie: No names in thread; use the CS list. Keep message factual and say ETA for next update 15m.

maria: Quick note — DNS TTL decrease to 30s would help but may take global propagation; cautious about churning. We'll keep current config and rely on weight + cache purge.

leo: After 18m, monitoring shows steady state: overall 5xx at 0.9% (baseline 0.4%). Keeping work items: verify provider completes evacuation, keep forced weight until provider clears, run a controlled reintroduce once fabric stable.

incident-bot: Status update posted to incident channel and pager log updated with mitigation steps.

raj: Marking incident as mitigated for customer impact. Defer full P1 postmortem. I'll collect logs and timeline. Thanks all — will update if anything regresses.

evan-cs: Closing CS loop for now. We'll tag impacted customers and prepare comms for postmortem.

sylvie: Final: incident resolved for now; root cause suspected provider L3 fabric disruption in us-east-1-a causing target health flaps and DNS/edge cache mismatch that prevented a clean automated traffic-shift. Postmortem to cover: timing of weight changes, TTL/cache behavior, traffic-shift controller resilience, and provider mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Owners: raj (oncall), maria (netops), leo (cloud-support), evan (cs). Postmortem owner: sylvie.
